decision: not retained: the special-case refinement fixes the measured zero-endpoint saturation, but an actual symmetric nonzero-endpoint producer still expands one necessary index visit to 65
resource_gate_scope: Early resource gate after focused validation; full production suites and report replay remain required before admission. Five fresh alternating processes per variant/mode on CPU 0 after 100 ms integer-only conditioning. Timing uses the system allocator; memory binaries separately count requested Rust allocations. Each exact full private index implementation is extracted verbatim and linked to its frozen production library; the private bounds wrapper is represented by the public STRICT wrapper. Nine prepared point workloads measure index construction, first, repeated and cloned-point queries. Point producer construction and query clones are outside measurement; selected-point certified equality checks run after measured queries. Independent box-overlap and known-point witnesses check every candidate output, including a conservative false-positive saturation control. Incorrect baseline omissions remain recorded as correctness deltas. This is an index microbenchmark, not complete public Boolean performance or an application speedup claim.

symmetric_endpoint_counterexample.scope: Actual production point constructors and public STRICT bounds feed the verbatim index. Both variants return the same correct conservative candidate [64], but the refined candidate needlessly visits 64 additional disjoint entries. This is a structural scan-count regression, not a matched timing measurement or a public Boolean wrong answer.
symmetric_endpoint_counterexample.independent_width: MAX/2 - (-MAX/2) is exactly MAX in both binary64 and real arithmetic.

next_step: Evaluate a general subtraction-residual upper bound instead of enumerating exact endpoint cases. Verify its width bounds with an independent exact rational oracle across subnormals, overflow boundaries, exponent gaps and cancellation before testing another production candidate.

research.limitation: The paper explicitly excludes overflow and underflow. Any use here must separately handle nonfinite intermediates and justify gradual-underflow behavior for addition/subtraction; no implementation or validation of that alternative is claimed yet.
research.license_reference: https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~quake/robust.html identifies the accompanying C implementation as public domain. No external code has been copied into production.
